title: The gate ladder: affected checks per task, the full gate and tree scanners per phase, CI under eight minutes
description: The same full set of checks runs per task, per phase, locally and in CI several times, and the set is large because the product carries its own tree lints as tests. Measured: a task gate in the dogfood plan took 716 s, of which the sweep was 384 s and the panel browser gate 282 s; a narrow task gate measured 1,327 s because derived affected steps re-ran 506 s of suites its own full-sweep key had already run; the sweep is 6 min 36 s of wall and 34.6 min of CPU, and CI runs take 12 to 15 minutes. The CI half of this ladder (one executable gate description, skip of a green SHA, the codec cells) is already the earlier F1 phase's; this phase adds the per-task and per-phase rungs and the remaining speed.
desiredOutcome: A task's gate is the selection of checks its change affects, trusted only after its miss rate was measured on this repository's history; tree scanners and the full gate, browser steps included, run once per phase and on push, never per task; a probe of the guarded lints runs at sign-off only when the phase changed them; the sweep's wall clock is under four minutes and CI is under eight minutes and 55 runner-minutes, each measured with the same command before and after; one commit verb writes the index and the shard together, so adding a task mid-phase never leaves the plan uncommittable; and red-first through a sweep-shaped command proves when the task's suites pass.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: acceptance (5) 'the measured result over 20 commits is recorded in the task outcome with the commit range'. The outcome records a 2-commit window (ad586f07b..d33730d60) in which one commit timed out at 1200s (NOT MEASURED) and the other was a full-set selection ('so no suite can be missed'), giving 'misses 0 of 1 commits (mutation); 0 of 1 runs (CI)'. That is zero evidence about the miss rate and not the 20-commit measurement the clause asks for; the executor itself says the 20-commit run is 'still owed by the orchestrator'. The 'misses 0 of 1' line must not be read as a clean miss rate.
findings.resolution: Run the 20-commit command the outcome names on a quiet machine (python3 tools/measure-affected-miss.py --commits 20 --budget-minutes 240 --timeout 2400 --ci-limit 30 --json) and record its output and commit range in the outcome before the task closes done; or, if the orchestrator decides the measurement is out of scope for this task, split it into its own task rather than close this one as met. If the task is closed with no change (--no-change --reason), the reason must say acceptance (5) is unmeasured.

findings.issue: P142.3's description is a verbatim re-ask of a task already done (b52ba79a, amended 66b3635d): tools/measure-affected-miss.py has existed since P131.16-dau, so this task adds nothing and its tests.add entries are met only by pre-existing cases m6, m8, m10, m13. A duplicate task in the plan is an input error that wastes an executor run and can double-count 'tests added'.
findings.resolution: Close P142.3 with --no-change and a reason naming b52ba79a/66b3635d and the pre-existing cases, after (5) is measured; or rewrite its description to the measurement alone.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "a phase touching no such file runs none and says so" / acceptance (2) "prints that it ran none" on the held path: a run that printed `ran none` is held as `state["lintProbe"] = {"head": head}` (the word is not stored), and the held branch then appends `lint probe green (held at this HEAD)` - so any re-entry at the same HEAD (e.g. after the sign-off verb stopped) reports a probe that ran no row as green, the exact reading-as-a-proof the clause forbids.
findings.resolution: Store the word with the hold (`{"head": head, "said": "ran none"|"green"}`) and echo it on the held branch (`lint probe ran none (held at this HEAD)`); add an lp6 twin that holds a ran-none run and asserts the held did-line says ran none.

findings.issue: The success print breaks the module's stated invariant `INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 300` ("The bound every print that is not a stop stays inside") whenever a probe runs: the executor's own measurement is 312 bytes in lp1's one-task fixture. This repo keeps tools/prove-gates.py, so from this change every sign-off here prints past the bound; lp1 does not assert the bound and dp3 only measures a probeless fixture, so nothing goes red.
findings.resolution: Make the probe clause fit (e.g. fold it into the `invariants clean` clause as `invariants clean, lint probe green|ran none`, or move the word into the sign-off summary) and extend dp3 (or lp1/lp2) to measure the success print of a probe-carrying fixture against INSTRUCTION_BYTES.

findings.issue: A shipped product script now executes any project file that happens to sit at `tools/prove-gates.py` at every sign-off, by filename convention alone, with no plan key opting in: a user project with an unrelated script at that path has it run with `--changed <paths>` and its exit 1 read as a not-proven stop and any other non-zero exit as a refusal that blocks sign-off. Every other gate the driver runs is named by the plan (meta.buildCommands, meta.runtimeBoot); this one is not. The executor flagged it as (b).
findings.resolution: Key the probe off the plan (a `meta.buildCommands` entry or a dedicated meta key naming the probe command and declaring it speaks the `--changed` protocol), absent means skip; set it in this repo's plan. If that is out of this task's files, file it as a fix task before sign-off rather than shipping the filename convention.

findings.issue: Acceptance (4) is checked as equality of porcelain status letters + paths only. A file already dirty before the run (` M`) that the probe leaves mutated still reads ` M` after, so a stranded mutation in an already-modified lint file passes; conversely, a second session editing the shared checkout during the minutes-long run produces a false `left the checkout changed` stop whose remedy (`restore the tree`) would tell the operator to discard someone else's work.
findings.resolution: For entries dirty before the run, also compare a content digest (git hash-object of each) before and after; and word the stop as 'changed during the probe run' naming the entries without prescribing a restore, or refuse to start the probe when a path in the changed set is already dirty.

findings.issue: `subprocess.run` of a minutes-long mutating probe carries no timeout, so a hung probe hangs the sign-off step indefinitely with the tree possibly mid-mutation.
findings.resolution: Pass a timeout (a generous bound or one read from the plan), catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` as a refusal stop; the status comparison in `finally` already reports what a killed run left.

findings.issue: lp6's 'at another HEAD it runs once' twin calls `lint_probe(..., None)`, which short-circuits the hold on `if head and ...`; it never exercises a different SHA, so a hold that ignored the head comparison (e.g. `held.get("head")` truthy) would still pass lp6.
findings.resolution: Call the twin with a different 40-hex head (`"b" * 40`) so the comparison itself is what lets it run.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Split each into staged blocks so the sweep spreads them across workers, and re-record the cost table.' The table is untouched, so the four split files keep the figures they had when each ran unsplit on one slot. Those figures now set the shard balance and every split file's timeout. On the live table, shard 3/3 holds three staged suites in a row (test_close_phase 330.3, test__deps 268.2, test_stamp_verification 265.4). The per-block process overhead on Windows, where test_stamp_verification now starts a process for each of its blocks, has never been measured. The executor gives a reason (the table binds to windows-latest and cannot be recorded from darwin), but the clause is still not done.
findings.resolution: Make it a tracked task before sign-off. Once this lands on a CI run, save each Windows selftests cell's log and run `python tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <logs> --platform windows-latest --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`. Then confirm that the shard split it prints is balanced and that no split file's calibrated timeout at held=3 sits within 2x of its measured wall time.

findings.file: tools/sweep-selftests.py:1361-1400 (the scheduler change); the bound is tests/test_drive_phase.py
findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Acceptance: (1) time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py is under 240 s wall on this machine twice, at least 20 minutes apart'. The executor measured 370.5 s and 370.9 s (20 min 11 s apart) and says itself that this is NOT MET. Its stated bound is test_drive_phase.py (about 209.6 s holding 6 of 8 slots; its blocks total 1343 process-seconds). The phase's desired outcome ('the sweep's wall clock is under four minutes') is therefore still open after this task.
findings.resolution: Open a follow-up task scoped to the bound the executor measured: cut the work in test_drive_phase.py's heaviest blocks, and/or add one cross-suite block pool in tests/_harness.py so blocks from different staged suites share the sweep's slots. Re-measure with the same command twice, 20 minutes apart. Alternatively, amend the description if 240 s is not reachable on this machine.

findings.issue: The diff makes three untouched documents state the old admission rule. CLAUDE.md says a staged suite 'is admitted with `stage_grant(jobs)` slots', CONTRIBUTING.md says 'is admitted holding `stage_grant(jobs)` slots', and the ci.yml comment says 'a staged suite is admitted holding all but one of them'. After slot_gate's change at tools/sweep-selftests.py:1385-1394, a suite holds as many slots as are free when its turn comes, between 1 and that number. The executor listed all three as stale and outside its files.
findings.resolution: Reword each to say: up to `stage_grant(jobs)` slots, as many as are free when its turn comes and at least one, with the number it holds passed to the child in SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT and its timeout calibrated to that number.

findings.issue: A staged suite's grant is fixed when it is admitted. If it is admitted with 1 slot, it runs every block serially (stage_workers=min(6,1)) for its whole run, even after other slots free up. Its timeout at held=1 is 3 x cost, which can exceed SWEEP_DEADLINE. tt5 still only bounds timeouts at the full grant, and its label was widened to accept that the deadline 'cuts ... a staged suite admitted late with fewer slots'. On today's windows table this is latent, not live. At jobs=4 the staged suite second in each shard gets 1 slot (shard 2/3: test_commit_task_work 222.9; shard 3/3: test__deps 268.2), and both serial costs are well under the 1380 s deadline. A rebalance that put test_audit_task (606.0) or test_drive_phase (1346.4) second in a shard would have the deadline cut a run that is slow, not hung, and nothing would turn red first.
findings.resolution: Add a tt5 sibling over the live table: for each `--shard i/3` at jobs=4, compute each staged suite's admitted slots (ticket order, with what is free at its turn, assuming earlier holders have not yet finished). Assert that file_timeout at those slots, and the serial cost it implies, stay under SWEEP_DEADLINE. That makes the latent case fail on the table change that creates it.

outcome.technical: CAUSE (reproduced, then established). Reproduction: a scratch repo at the parent of the P131.11 commit with that commit's three files laid over, `stamp-verification.py red --manifest docs/audit/audit-plan.json --task P131.11 -- python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/release.py tools/check-example-pins.py` read could-not-prove with 'with the working tree's implementation the task's tests do not all pass (no tally or error reader matched its output ...)'. The same sweep run directly in that tree printed only per-file 'ok' lines and the summary '2/2 files ok, 67 cases', exit 0; `_runner_output.read_run_tally` on that text returned None. So the reader that rejects the fix-side output is `fix_problem` (via `read_run_tally`): the sweep drops a green file's own output, so a passing sweep carries NO runner tally, only its own summary, which no reader read. Not the environment (the isolated run exits 0, 9.7s total) and not the time budget (nothing timed out). A SECOND blocker sat behind the first, hidden because fix_problem short-circuits before credit: the failing cases were located in the one script the command ran, which for a sweep is tools/sweep-selftests.py, not the suite, so every case read 'the runner locates it in no declared test file' (seen in the swc1 fixture after fixing the first), and the sweep's own two-space 'FAIL  <path>: <why>' lines were counted as failing house cases. FIX. _runner_output.py: `sweep_tally` (a sweep that graded every file ok, at least one file and one case; read_run_tally falls back to it LAST, behind every runner), `sweep_failing_cases` (house cases read per '--- path: why ---' block, each tagged with `script`), and `_house_cases` no longer reads the sweep's two-space FAIL lines. stamp-verification.py: `_failing_cases` (uses the per-file reader for a sweep-shaped command), `case_site` locates a house case at its block's script, `fix_problem` names the failing file ('the sweep failed tests/x.py (exited 1)'), `_TALLY_KEYS` row for the sweep, and the time budget: `sweep_suites`, `load_sweep_costs`, `sweep_budget`, `budget_clause` - for a command running tools/sweep-selftests.py over named suites, the recorded slot-seconds of those suites (read from .github/sweep-costs.json of the project, rounded up, never more than half the deadline) are held back from the baseline/task/held/second runs (`early` deadline) so the fix run keeps them; a suite with no recorded cost holds nothing and is named ('no recorded cost for X'); an unreadable table says why; the basis carries the clause. tools/sweep-selftests.py was NOT touched (its output shape was sufficient). EVIDENCE. Filed P131.11 case, re-run with its own command on the fixed helper in the scratch repo: status proved ('3 of 43 collected tests failing an assertion ... x5, x6, rl16 ... each passing with the working tree's implementation ... fix run: held back 3s of the deadline, the recorded slot-seconds of tools/check-example-pins.py in .github/sweep-costs.json; no recorded cost for tools/release.py') in 10.5s. Cases: swc1-swc9 in tests/test_stamp_verification.py (new stage swc-block, 9/9), rs3 and rs4 in tests/test__runner_output.py (22/22). Red first: before any fix swc1, swc2, swc3 failed on the fixture (swc1 read could-not-prove, the pre-fix behaviour) and the rest raised on the missing symbols. Mutations on a scratch copy (not the tree), each restored, pycache purged: fix_problem accepts any exit 0 -> swc3 red; sweep_tally accepts partial/empty sweeps -> swc3, swc4, rs4 red; sweep_tally never fires -> swc1, swc3, swc4, swc8, rs4 red; fix_problem drops the failing-file clause -> swc2 red; case_site ignores the block script -> swc1, swc8 red; early deadline = deadline -> swc9 red; default 60s cost for an uncosted suite -> swc5, swc6, swc7, swc9 red; _house_cases reads the two-space FAIL lines -> rs3 red. Gate: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py tests/test__runner_output.py tests/test_run_test_gate.py tests/test__filed_returns.py --jobs 4 --quiet` -> '4/4 files ok, 1025 cases' (summary line read; this was the sweep's own tail, the pipe hides its exit code, so the summary is the evidence). ruff check on the three changed areas: All checks passed; vermin -t=3.8-: exit 0; _output_lints.prose_number_claims() and house_style_violations() over the tree: [] and []. Names used elsewhere (_build_throwaway, _decisive_line, _hard_link_or_copy, _head_text): untouched. _runner_output.py's dependants (run-test-gate.py, stamp-verification.py, test__refs.py, test__runner_output.py, test_run_test_gate.py, test_stamp_verification.py, test__filed_returns.py): still correct - run-test-gate.py uses sweep_failures/sweep_summary/SWEEP_RUNNER, all unchanged; read_run_tally's only change is a last-resort fallback that returns a tally only for a clean sweep summary, so no other runner's output changes (rs4 pins that a runner's own tally wins); the one behavioural change under a shared reader is `_house_cases` skipping lines that begin with 'FAIL' plus two spaces, which the harness never prints (its line is 'FAIL <label>'); test_run_test_gate.py and test__filed_returns.py ran green. _json_blob, _unittest_cases, _vitest_cases, playwright_line_cases: untouched. tests/test_stamp_verification.py's dependants (sweep-costs.json, test__filed_returns.py, sweep-selftests.py, verify.sh): still correct - only an added stage; the sweep-costs.json row for the suite is unchanged by this task (a re-record is the orchestrator's call; the suite grew by one stage). tools/sweep-selftests.py: untouched, so its 42 dependants are unaffected. tests/test__runner_output.py: two cases added; its cost row and the guide reference stand. tasks.title: The affected selection's miss rate is measured on this repository's history before any task gate trusts it
tasks.description: Add tools/measure-affected-miss.py. Mutation half: for each of the last N task commits (default 20), in a scratch worktree at that commit, apply each of two mutations to every changed .py (an import-time raise, and a house-style violation the tree lints read), run the full sweep, and count the suites that went red that tools/affected.py --base <parent> did not select. CI half: for each failed CI run in the window, read its failing suites (gh run view --log-failed) and check them against the selection for that SHA's diff. It prints 'misses M of N commits (mutation); K of J runs (CI)' with every miss named; a CI half that could not ask prints could-not-ask and is never read as zero. It never edits the checkout: every mutation happens in its own scratch worktree, removed in finally. Acceptance: (1) on a fixture repository where a suite depends on a changed module the selection omits, the miss is counted and named; (2) a selection that includes every red suite counts zero misses; (3) no gh, or no network, prints could-not-ask for the CI half; (4) the checkout's status is unchanged after a run; (5) the measured result over 20 commits is recorded in the task outcome with the commit range.

tasks.title: Runner output read off a Windows pipe keeps CRLF, and every reader anchored at end of line stops matching
tasks.description:
CI release tier on ci/P142 (run 40194747670, sha 4805f994) is red on Windows only: tests/test_stamp_verification.py cases swc1, swc2, swc8 fail on windows plain, windows cp1252 and resample. Cause, reproduced on macOS: stamp-verification decodes a run's stdout as bytes (`.decode("utf-8", "replace")`), so a Windows child's `\r\n` survives into the text, and `_runner_output` readers anchored with `[ \t]*$` under re.M stop matching - `sweep_tally("...1/1 files ok, 2 cases\r\n")` returns None while the LF twin returns the tally. The pytest reader survives only because its regex does not anchor at end of line; jest/vitest/mocha/sweep/FAIL-line readers share the defect.

This is a class, not the sweep instance: fix it once at the entry every reader already goes through - `plain_text()` (it strips terminal escapes "once, here") - by normalising `\r\n` and lone `\r` line ends to `\n`, and update its docstring to state both normalisations. Then check every public reader in `_runner_output` actually reaches `plain_text` before matching; any that does not, route it through.

tasks.title: The affected selection names every suite a change can turn red: tree-scanning lints always, and suites reaching a module through a subprocess or a sibling's import
tasks.description:
The P142.3 measurement (tools/measure-affected-miss.py --commits 20, range 17563b1b..4805f994) found that 13 of 16 measured commits had at least one suite turned red by a mutation in a changed file that tools/affected.py did not select. Two classes, not a list of instances:

1. Tree-scanning suites. A suite whose lint walks every tracked file (tests/test__output_lints.py on a style mutation in almost every commit; also test__help_lints, test__deps, test__refs and the like) is affected by ANY change to a file in the set it scans. The selection must derive that set from the lint's own walk (the shared walks in tools/lints) rather than from a hand list, and select the suite whenever a changed path falls inside it.
2. Reach the import graph does not show. Raise mutations were missed for suites that reach the module transitively (A imports B imports changed C), through a subprocess of an entry script (`[sys.executable, <script>]`, `_loader`, `find_script`), or by reading its source. Close the reverse-import walk transitively and add the subprocess/loader edges, derived from the code, not spelled.

Acceptance: (1) every (commit, missed suite) pair the measurement JSON recorded is selected when tools/affected.py is given that commit's changed files - write the cases from that data, so they fail on today's code; (2) the selection stays narrower than the full sweep for a commit that touches one leaf module (report the count, do not assert a number in prose); (3) measure-affected-miss.py keeps its CLI; if it needs a flag to read the selection, add it. The re-measurement over >=20 commits is NOT part of this task - the orchestrator runs it on a quiet machine afterwards.

Measurement data: <scratchpad>/miss-rate-20.json, the orchestrator hands over the full path (read-only; per commit: sha, changed, mutations[].missed).

No F/P/BUG ids in comments. Do not run the full measurement or any browser gate.

tasks.title: The sweep finishes under four minutes: the costliest staged suite does less work, and the sweep's workers run blocks from every staged suite
tasks.description:
P142.8 split four suites into staged blocks and changed the slot gate; the sweep went from 430.6 s / 418.3 s to 370.5 s / 370.9 s (two runs each, 20 min gap, 8 slots on a 10-core machine), short of the 240 s acceptance. Its measured bound: about 2200 CPU-seconds of total work over 8 slots cannot finish under about 275 s even with perfect packing, and tests/test_drive_phase.py alone holds 6 of 8 slots for about 210 s (113 blocks, 1343 process-seconds).

Two parts, both needed:
1. Less work in tests/test_drive_phase.py: find what its blocks repeat (fixture repositories built per block, full drive runs where a function call answers the same question) and share or narrow it without dropping a case. Report process-seconds before and after.
2. Blocks, not suites, as the unit the sweep schedules: let the sweep's workers draw individual blocks from every staged suite (tests/_harness.py staged_main and the runner's slot gate) so one large suite no longer holds a fixed grant while others wait. Keep per-block timeouts calibrated, keep each block's scratch-dir isolation and the watched-pair checks, and keep --shard I/N balancing working with .github/sweep-costs.json.

Acceptance: (1) `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` wall clock under 240 s, measured twice with a gap before and after, spread reported; (2) the case count per file is unchanged (print both); (3) the runner's own suite and tests/test__harness.py cover the block scheduling, red-first by breaking it; (4) no number written into prose. The Windows cost table is re-recorded by the orchestrator from CI logs, not here.

No F/P/BUG ids in comments. No browser gates.

tasks.title: The sign-off lint probe is named by the plan, reports a held run by what it did, fits the print budget, and bounds and scopes its restore check
tasks.description:
Review findings on the sign-off lint probe that P142.6 added to drive-phase.py `lint_probe()` (fix them together, they share the function):
- R3 (med): the hold stores only the HEAD, so a re-entry at the same HEAD after a run that printed `ran none` reports `lint probe green (held at this HEAD)`. Store the outcome word with the hold and print it back; a held ran-none run says ran none.
- R4 (med): the success print is over INSTRUCTION_BYTES (300) with the probe clause. Shorten or merge the clause so every non-stop print fits, and make the byte-budget case measure a fixture that HAS a probe.
- R5 (med): the shipped driver runs whatever sits at the hard-coded `tools/prove-gates.py`. The probe must be named by the plan: read a `meta.buildCommands` key (name it `lintProbe`; the driver appends `--changed <paths>`), and a plan without the key skips the step and says so in the did-line. The orchestrator sets the key on this repo's plan with `/audit:task build-command`; do not edit docs/audit.
- R6 (low): the restore check compares status letters only; compare contents (hash) of files already modified before the run, and word the stop so it does not tell the operator to discard another session's edits.
- R7 (low): give the probe run a timeout derived from the drive's own budget, and report a timeout as a stop naming it.
- R8 (low): lp6's other-HEAD twin passes head=None; use a different SHA so a hold that ignores the head goes red.
Update phase-signoff.md step 4b to match. Red-first each case against today's code. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

openChoices: The selection's miss rate is read from two sources: a mutation replay over recent task commits and the real red runs in CI's history. Whether a miss in either blocks trusting the selection, or only a real one, is the owner's call; the recommendation is either
Tree scanners leave task gates: a task that breaks a whole-tree lint lands red on its phase branch until the phase gate catches it before merge

The browser gates stay with the orchestrator and run serially; a task gate includes them only when the selection says the surface changed
